newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst, BASF detail joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst, BASF detail joint venture.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Monday that its planned polypropylene joint venture with Hoechst AG will be called Targor and begin operations on July 1.
The new group, to be sited in Mainz, Germany will have an annual production capacity of 1.4 million tonnes of propylene, used to make automobile parts, certain foils, and other plastic goods.
Production sites will be in Knapsack near Cologne, in Lillebonne, France, Wilton, U.K., Rozenburg, the Netherlands, and Tarragona, Spain.
Polypropylene production capacities at the Rheinische Olefinwerke in Wesseling, a joint-venture run between BASF and Shell, will be used on a loan basis.
Last year Hoechst posted sales of 900 million marks while BASF posted sales of 800 million marks in this business area.
